expert: Target user: crypto/futures trader on X (40k followers, X Premium, 3-6 posts a day, paid Telegram; churned from Typefully and Hypefury)

typefully-a.verdict: The only one where the rewrite sounds like a CT account and not a LinkedIn post. I'd tap Start free.
typefully-a.loved: The hero example is the classic CT flex: 'just wanted to share that i finally hit my first $10k month trading, took me 3 years lol' becomes 'my first $10k month trading took me 3 years.' It stays lowercase, and the receipt says 'Kept: $10k · 3 years · your lowercase'. That's exactly what I'd have done. The locked, greyed-out toggles ('Auto-DMs: Not a setting. Not ever.') look like real app settings, so I believe them more than a slogan.
problems: In the first second it looks like Typefully (dark, blue, lowercase 'hook' + italic 'worthy'). I churned from that, so my first thought is 'another one'.
'Try it here' underlined my BTC line ('5 soft words') and then told me the rewrite 'runs in the app'. I never see whether it beats MY hook.
'Make it hookworthy.' is a brand pun, set in low-contrast grey on a phone. The pain is in line 1. Line 2 does nothing.

The voice-note draft 'it isn't. it's how you stay in the game' is the it's-not-X-it's-Y cadence everyone now reads as AI. And '15 auto-posts a month' in pricing sits right after 'Auto-reposts: never'.
typefully-a.fix: Let 'Try it here' actually rewrite one line I paste, with no signup, and show the receipt. Seeing my own line come back sharper is the moment I convert.

arc-b.verdict: Clearest before/after on a phone and the best trust receipt, but the cream and pastel look reads 'Substack', not 'CT'.
arc-b.loved: Red strikethrough on 'so i think' / 'honestly just', then the lime-highlighted rewrite, all inside 2 seconds. I got it before I scrolled. And the 'WILL IT EVER, ON ITS OWN… AUTO-DMS NEVER / AUTO-REPOSTS NEVER / POSTS YOU SENT: ALL OF THEM' receipt is the exact answer to why I left Hypefury.
problems: Warm paper with yellow, lavender, mint and peach cards feels like a newsletter or Canva creator tool. Everyone on CT lives in dark mode.

Typing my own line into 'Try yours': the wavy underlines drift off the words once it wraps to 3 lines, the start of my line scrolls out of view, and 'Sharpen it free' gives a soft-spot list plus 'Tap Sharpen in the app' instead of a rewrite.

The hero before-line is a straw man nobody with an audience writes, and the rewrite turns lowercase into Title-ish Case ('Most underrated thing in trading? Sizing down after a loss.'). That's the opposite of 'still sounds like you' for a lowercase account.
Five candy-colour receipt cards in a row get long on a phone. By the third I'm skimming.
arc-b.fix: Keep the strikethrough-to-highlighter hero and the NEVER receipt, but put it on a dark ground and lead with a lowercase example that stays lowercase.

apple-b.verdict: The hero post is the most 'real trader' thing on any of the five, and the product's own sample thread ends in a ChatGPT line.
apple-b.loved: 'I lost $4,000 in March doubling my size to win it back. Now I cut size in half after any red day.' That's revenge sizing, a real number, a real rule. It's what I actually post, sitting in a feed, under 'Write the line they stop for.', so I get scroll-stopping in one second.
problems: The sample thread ends 'It's not a strategy. It's a seatbelt.' That's the textbook AI construction. If that's what the tool writes, I'm out.
The before-line is a tiny grey truncated strikethrough ('so i think the most underrated thing in trading i…') you can't read on a phone, so the change is invisible.
No sticky header after the hero. When I'm convinced halfway down, there's no Start free under my thumb.

Below the hero it goes generic ('Any niche. Same fix.'). The '309/280, becomes a thread of 2' pitch is irrelevant to Premium accounts. And the 'example account, feed is illustrative' pill reads like legal fine print over the demo.
apple-b.fix: Rewrite the sample thread's last line into something blunt and human, and make the before-line readable in full above the sharpened version.

arc-a.verdict: Safe and clear. The sticker peel sells the one tap, but the rest looks like every blue SaaS page I've already scrolled past.
arc-a.loved: The amber stickers 'so i think the' and 'is honestly just' peel off and lie under the sharpened line. I can see exactly what got cut, on a trading line, in the first screen. Down the page, 'Took the loss, cut size in half, slept fine. That's the whole edge.' sounds like a real trader.
problems: Stock photos: a laptop under a lamp, founders laughing over pizza, a sticky-note wall. Pure template energy, and it kills the 'real people' feel.
'Good ideas die in bad first lines.' is a copywriter line, not my pain. 'They read one line' or 'X pays for posts' would hit harder.
The hero rewrite capitalises a lowercase voice, which contradicts 'It still sounds like you.'
Pricing lists '15 auto-posts a month' right after the crossed-out 'Auto-reposts'. If you're skimming, that reads as a contradiction.
arc-a.fix: Replace the stock-photo audience cards with real-looking X posts (a PnL-card post, a sizing thread), and rename 'auto-posts' to 'scheduled posts'.

awwwards-b.verdict: Pretty, but it's an English teacher marking my tweet in blue pencil. Not my world.
awwwards-b.loved: The 'SENT BY YOU' stamp over the handwritten 'never' list (Auto-DMs, Auto-replies, Auto-deletes, Auto-reposts) is the most human trust moment of the five.
problems: Typewriter mono and proofreader's marks feel like homework being graded. It's built for newsletter writers, not someone posting a chart at the open.
The marks draw in slowly. At 0.5s the hero card is unmarked typewriter text, and on a fast thumb-scroll the paper cards sit half-empty.
Mono ALL-CAPS buttons ('SHARPEN MY FIRST POST') and the small typewriter body are hard to read at phone size.
Same straw-man hero line, and the rewrite capitalises it.
awwwards-b.fix: Drop the typewriter body text for the post itself and show the rewrite as a real X post, so the edit marks read as a feature rather than a grading session.

pickWhy: It's the only one whose hero rewrite keeps my lowercase and kills the fluff without turning me into a LinkedIn post, and it lives in dark mode like my feed. The locked toggles and the 'no hero trades in between' reply make me believe it won't touch my account or my voice.
combo: Take typefully-a's dark page and $10k example. Add arc-b's strikethrough-to-highlighter before/after and its 'WILL IT EVER, ON ITS OWN… NEVER' receipt. Use apple-b's '$4,000 doubling my size' body copy as the second example.
